chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Ja‘far al-Razzāz narrated to me from his uncle Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Zayyāt, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā‘īl, from Ṣāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from Abī Hārūn al-Makfūf, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said – as part of a longer ḥadīth: "Whoever is mentioned al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) in his presence, and tears flow from his eye [or eyes] the size of a fly's wing, his reward is with Allāh, the Mighty and Majestic, and He will not be satisfied for him with less than Paradise."

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ: Imam al-Husayn, the grandson of the Prophet
key_terms.جَنَاحِ ذُبَابٍ: The wing of a fly (used as a measure of small quantity)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for crying when hearing about Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this tradition from Abū Hārūn al-Makfūf, highlighting that even a microscopic emotional response—tears the size of a fly's wing—upon hearing the name of Imām al-Ḥusayn (a.s.) secures Paradise. This underscores the Shia emphasis on *al-walāʾ* (affection) for the Ahl al-Bayt as a decisive criterion for salvation, where genuine emotional resonance outweighs ritual volume. The minimal threshold illustrates that sincerity of heart in remembering the tragedy of Karbala is sufficient for divine acceptance.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz narrated to me from his uncle Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain Al-Zayyāt, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl, from Sāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from Abī Hārūn Al-Makfūf, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said – as part of a longer Ḥadīth: Those who shed tears when Ḥusain (a.s.) is mentioned in front of them will be rewarded by Allāh Himself, even if their tears are as small as the wing of a fly. And Allāh will not be pleased with any reward for them less than Paradise.
